teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.desc: A young, hard-playing team without the talent to compete every week, coming off a blowout loss at Denver. Writers point to quarterback questions and a tough stretch of road games. Tight end Trey McBride's big season is the bright spot.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.desc: The upset of San Francisco, sealed by rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels's interception, earned attention. Michael Penix Jr. looks comfortable, and the defense is making plays. Writers are still unsure how real it is.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.desc: Without Lamar Jackson, the offense has stalled after halftime and Baltimore has blown leads in every loss. The defense collapsed against Cincinnati. The season is seen as hinging on Jackson's return and the upcoming games at Buffalo and against Jacksonville.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.desc: Josh Allen and the league's top scoring offense keep Buffalo near the top, and two outlets moved the Bills to No. 1 without playing. Receiver DJ Moore's speed is opening up the offense. The defense is the common worry heading into a big test against Baltimore.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.desc: The 43–13 loss to Tampa Bay cooled the hype around Bryce Young and the division lead. Turnovers and a run defense that is last in the league are the common themes. Linebacker Devin Lloyd is the bright spot on defense.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.desc: Caleb Williams is the story: writers say he is far more accurate and playing his best football since returning. The defense is improving but still has holes, with safety Dillon Thieneman helping steady the secondary. Monday night in Seattle is seen as the test, and the rankings came out before the Jeffery Simmons trade.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.desc: Joe Burrow's dominant second half against Baltimore, 35 unanswered points, has writers talking about his MVP case. Receiver Ja'Marr Chase's halftime speech gets credit for sparking the turnaround. Consistency is the open question for a team that has been up and down.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.desc: Deshaun Watson's late drives keep producing wins, and first-year coach Todd Monken gets credit for a tough, resilient team. A sweep of Pittsburgh would put them in control of the AFC North. Some writers doubt the close-game streak can last.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.desc: The offense looked like itself in the Monday night win at Philadelphia, led by Javonte Williams's big rushing night. The defense, especially against the run, is still the problem. Writers see real progress but not a finished team.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.desc: Bo Nix and the offense finally broke out against Arizona, and the defense keeps improving. Receiver Jaylen Waddle leads the team in catches and yards. Some writers are still not sold on Nix, and injuries are starting to pile up.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.desc: Jared Goff and the offense are humming, and safety Brian Branch's return helps the defense. The defense giving games away is the recurring theme. Writers also wonder how Goff will handle Minnesota's defense next.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.desc: Writers split the blame for the Detroit loss between officiating and Green Bay's own mistakes in the red zone and on special teams. Jordan Love and a defense that leads the league in takeaways keep them respected. Thursday against Carolina is about avoiding a second straight loss.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.desc: The overtime loss to the Giants hurt, and writers keep asking how a once-elite defense fell off so quickly. C.J. Stroud keeps them competitive. The margin for error in the AFC South is gone.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.desc: Three straight losses have writers calling the season over, and the Nelson and Buckner trades confirmed a rebuild. Persistent mistakes, including Daniel Jones's interceptions, deepen the slide. Jonathan Taylor is the bright spot.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.desc: Seen as a top-10 team that stumbled in a last-second London loss, with a manageable schedule ahead. A season-ending injury to tackle Anton Harrison is the main concern. Some writers also question why receiver Brian Thomas Jr.'s role has shrunk.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.desc: The 20–3 loss in Seattle exposed an offense without a big-play receiver. Several writers say Patrick Mahomes needs help before the trade deadline. Running back Kenneth Walker III has eased the load, but the soft early schedule gets mentioned too.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.desc: The league's only winless team, far below preseason expectations as a Super Bowl sleeper. The bye did not fix the offense. A tough three-game stretch is next.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.desc: The run game came back with nearly 200 yards in a win over Las Vegas. Writers like the talent but want to see it again before buying in, especially with Davante Adams out and an inconsistent defense.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.desc: Four straight losses after a 3–0 start have writers calling the hot start a mirage. The defense allows the most points in the league. The main debate is when rookie Fernando Mendoza replaces Kirk Cousins at quarterback.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.desc: The first win of the season, over the Jets, was a needed lift for a rebuilding team. Malik Willis played well and the young players keep improving. Writers still expect tougher weeks ahead with a thin roster.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.desc: The league's last unbeaten team climbed to the top on the strength of an elite defense under coordinator Brian Flores. The shared knock is an offense that barely functions, with uneven quarterback play from Kyler Murray. Writers also flag a tough four-game stretch ahead as the real test.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.desc: Drake Maye is playing well, and writers respect a 4–3 record through injuries. Turnovers, the run game, and defensive lapses in the loss at Chicago keep them out of the top tier. A.J. Brown's role in the offense is flagged as something to fix.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.desc: The effort is there but the talent is not, with no run game and missed kicks. Injuries have them losing four of five. Kellen Moore's job security comes up often.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.desc: The overtime win over Houston has the Giants atop a weak NFC East and among the most entertaining teams to watch. J.J. McCarthy's play and the run game, led by Cam Skattebo's 124 yards, are a big part of the buzz. John Harbaugh's new culture gets credit too.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.desc: The loss to previously winless Miami was the low point, and writers are openly questioning Aaron Glenn's job. The Jets keep wasting good individual efforts with late mistakes. Rookie pass rusher David Bailey is a bright spot.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.desc: Injuries and five straight losses have writers calling the season nearly over. Saquon Barkley was rushed back and hurt again. Sunday night at Washington is framed as a must-win, with talk of a possible fire sale.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.desc: Winning ugly but winning, with Aaron Rodgers executing Mike McCarthy's adjustments and a strong running back duo led by Jaylen Warren. They are tied for the division lead. Sunday against Cleveland is framed as close to a must-win.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.desc: Writers everywhere credit the defense that shut down Kansas City and a run game revived by Emanuel Wilson. The doubts center on Sam Darnold and whether the offense has enough playmakers. Most rankings came out before the Quenton Nelson trade, and Monday's game against the Bears is framed as the next big test.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.desc: Most writers forgave the loss at Atlanta, pinning it on injuries, a short week, and four turnovers. The bye is seen as perfectly timed, and the 49ers are expected to climb back as players return. Receiver Mike Evans gets credit for lifting Brock Purdy's production when he plays.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.desc: The blowout of Carolina, powered by Bucky Irving and the run game and a dominant defense, revived their NFC South hopes. Writers see a team becoming competent again with Baker Mayfield back. The division is still there for the taking.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.desc: At 1–6 with a struggling defense, Tennessee shows signs of life in Cam Ward and Tony Pollard. Writers doubt they can string wins together. The Titans traded star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago after these rankings came out.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.desc: Dan Quinn is under pressure coming off the bye, now without Terry McLaurin for the season. The defense allows too many points. Washington is still technically in the division race, and rookie receiver Antonio Williams gets a bigger chance.

9.title: Week 9 Power Rankings: Who's Still Standing?

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.desc: Gardner Minshew came off the bench and sparked an overtime comeback win at Dallas, earning the starting job. Writers see it as a short-term fix for a team with real quarterback questions, but the win moved Arizona up six spots in the consensus.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.desc: Atlanta lost 16-0 to Tampa Bay without the Buccaneers completing a pass, a result that left writers pointing to both the run defense and Michael Penix Jr.'s accuracy problems. A brutal upcoming schedule stretches ahead. The NFC South race remains alive but the arrow points down.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.desc: Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve with a thumb injury, and writers are calling Baltimore's playoff hopes in serious jeopardy. Tyler Huntley is the fallback option, and the upcoming home game against Jacksonville is viewed as a likely loss. Sellers at the deadline is the emerging consensus.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.desc: Buffalo sits atop every editorial list this week, the only team ranked first across the most outlets of any team on the board. Writers point to Josh Allen and the top-scoring offense, though the defense still draws questions ahead of a road test at Minnesota.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.desc: Carolina is still atop the NFC South despite two straight losses and the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. Bryce Young's recent struggles after a strong start are the common concern. A home game against Denver is framed as a critical gut-check.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.desc: The Jeffery Simmons trade paid off immediately, with the defensive tackle helping Chicago dominate Seattle on the road. Writers see the Bears as a legitimate NFC contender now that Caleb Williams has the defense to match the offense.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.desc: Cincinnati is 9th-10th across all nine outlets, with Joe Burrow coming through late in an overtime win over Tennessee. Writers see the offense as elite when Burrow is on but flag the defense as the ceiling-setter for a team with real AFC North ambitions.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.desc: Cleveland's loss to Pittsburgh, where Deshaun Watson was sacked eight times, raised fresh doubts about the offensive line. Writers still respect a 5-3 record and a defense that keeps games close, but the dominant win still hasn't materialized.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.desc: Dallas blew a 17-point lead at home to Arizona in a loss that writers called one of the most frustrating of the season. Jerry Jones ruled out a coaching change, and writers question whether the passing-focused offense can fix a leaky defense without scheme changes.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.desc: Denver wins close games and took the AFC West lead by beating Kansas City. The offense is improving, though writers note Denver was outgained in the win. The upcoming trip to Carolina is seen as a chance to separate from the AFC pack.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.desc: Detroit rallied past Minnesota with a late touchdown drive and held the previous top team to a poor offensive showing. The defense has allowed 17 points or fewer in consecutive games, and safety Brian Branch's return is a big part of the turnaround.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.desc: Green Bay improved to 5-3 with a defense that is tightening under Jonathan Gannon. Jordan Love and improving depth keep writers respectful, and Micah Parsons is practicing and could return. The run game's inconsistency is the persistent knock.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.desc: Houston is on its bye after a defense that once ranked elite has allowed the most points in the league over the past four weeks. C.J. Stroud keeps the offense functional, and writers see the upcoming schedule as a path back toward relevance.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.desc: Three straight losses and the Nelson and Buckner trades confirm a rebuild underway in Indianapolis. The 42-7 blowout loss to Jacksonville was the most recent reminder of the talent gap. Jonathan Taylor remains the team's most watchable player.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.desc: Jacksonville sits in the top seven at every outlet, with writers pointing to a top-10 scoring offense and scoring defense and the AFC's best point differential. Trevor Lawrence is drawing MVP conversation, and the AFC South looks like Jacksonville's to win.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.desc: Two straight losses have writers noting the Chiefs' run game has stalled and their secondary is thin. Patrick Mahomes keeps them near the top, and writers expect a bounce-back against the Jets. Kenneth Walker's health is the key variable.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.desc: Los Angeles is 0-7 and writers have run out of charitable things to say. A loss to the Rams in which the team generated no momentum has renewed questions about whether Justin Herbert is the right long-term answer. Bottom of the rankings at all nine outlets.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.desc: Back-to-back wins and back to .500, with the two-back run game and Puka Nacua leading a healthy-enough offense. Writers still flag a leaky defense and a roster without a full complement of starters. Myles Garrett's potential return is the upside trigger.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.desc: Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a comeback win over the Jets, with Kirk Cousins playing well and rookie Mike Washington Jr. emerging at running back. The defense giving up 439 yards in a win keeps writers skeptical about sustainability.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.desc: Miami led New England 13-3 at halftime and lost, extending a disappointing season. Writers see Malik Willis and younger players improving week to week but do not project wins against tougher competition. The roster remains thin.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.desc: Minnesota's first loss of the season, at Detroit, dropped the Vikings off the top spot at every outlet. Writers point to offensive struggles with Kyler Murray and a defense that gave up a late lead. A home game against Buffalo is framed as the season's biggest test.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.desc: New England won at Miami with a strong second half but did not look sharp in the first. Drake Maye and the defense keep the Patriots in the top 12 across all nine outlets. A home game against Green Bay is framed as the next meaningful measuring stick.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.desc: New Orleans is on its bye after losing four of five, with writers pointing to no run game, missed kicks, and mounting injuries. Kellen Moore's job security comes up repeatedly. A home game against Cleveland is next.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.desc: J.J. McCarthy led an overtime win at Houston, and writers credit John Harbaugh's coaching for a team trending upward despite losing Jaxson Dart. The Giants lead a weak NFC East. The floor is real, but several outlets see the ceiling as still unknown.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.desc: New York lost to Las Vegas despite leading in yards and generating good individual efforts, with writers pointing to late mistakes and Aaron Glenn's coaching under growing scrutiny. Rookie pass rusher David Bailey is the one consistent bright spot in a 2-6 season.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.desc: Philadelphia's season is being called a disaster across multiple outlets, with five straight losses and Saquon Barkley injured again. Writers are openly discussing a potential sell-off before the trade deadline.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.desc: Pittsburgh blew out Cleveland and took the AFC North lead heading into its bye. Writers credit a rejuvenated pass rush and run game, with Aaron Rodgers executing efficiently. Several outlets note the team could be a buyer at the trade deadline for receiver help.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.desc: Seattle dropped four to five spots at most outlets after losing at home to Chicago and struggling to generate offense. Sam Darnold's issues under pressure and third-down failures are the common themes. The earlier win over Kansas City is being revisited as a possible outlier.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.desc: San Francisco returns from the bye firmly in the top five across all nine outlets, with the DeForest Buckner trade seen as shoring up a defensive line that needed help. Writers expect the 49ers to climb once injured receivers return.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.desc: Two straight wins powered entirely by the run game, including a 322-yard rushing performance without completing a pass. Baker Mayfield barely threw, and writers see the defense improving. Best team in the NFC South is now the prevailing take.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.desc: Cam Ward had his best game against Cincinnati despite the overtime loss, and Tony Pollard gives the offense a weapon. Tennessee is 1-7 and the defense is poor, but writers are starting to note the team is competitive even when it loses.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.desc: Jayden Daniels earned Washington's first win of the year against Philadelphia, and writers see him running the offense efficiently. The performance was not convincing enough to move Washington into the top 20, but the arrow is pointing up after weeks of struggles.

10.title: Four NFC North Teams in the Top 10

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.desc: The Cardinals lost Jeremiyah Love to injured reserve and failed to score a touchdown against Seattle, leaving their offense dangerously thin at skill positions. With rookie Carson Beck likely making his debut after Gardner Minshew II's season-ending injury, Arizona is in full rebuild mode at 3-6.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.desc: Michael Penix Jr. has struggled badly against pressure, stalling an offense that has real talent around it. At 3-5-1, the Falcons have dropped four of five and face a tough schedule, with their playoff window closing fast.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.desc: Lamar Jackson is working back from a thumb injury, and the Ravens traded for Jacoby Brissett to stabilize things in the meantime. At 4-5 with only a 2.7% playoff probability per ESPN, Baltimore faces a potential new low with the winless Chargers on Monday Night Football.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.desc: The Bills won a physical road game at Minnesota and sit at 7-1, with writers pointing to their ability to grind out wins as a sign they can go deep in January. A Christmas rematch with Denver could decide AFC home-field advantage, making their remaining schedule critical.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.desc: Carolina fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, but writers note the pass rush and effort issues go beyond coaching. At 3-5 the Panthers have three winnable NFC South games ahead and are still alive in the playoff race, though the offense has been inconsistent.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.desc: The Bears overcame five turnovers to beat Tampa Bay, which Bleacher Report sees as a hallmark of a team capable of a title run. At 7-2 Chicago leads the NFC, with a Christmas game against Green Bay carrying major tiebreaker weight in the NFC North.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.desc: The Bengals have won four straight with Joe Burrow playing at an MVP level, and ESPN's FPI favors them in every remaining game. A Week 14 showdown with Kansas City could be the moment Cincinnati locks in its Super Bowl belief.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.desc: Cleveland has dropped two straight and faces a potential quarterback controversy between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders. The Browns sit at 5-4 with a Week 18 finale at Cincinnati that could carry AFC North and playoff implications.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.desc: Dallas got a needed win over Indianapolis despite 14 penalties and a shaky defense, keeping the Cowboys at 4-5 and still technically in the NFC East hunt. Writers are skeptical a deep postseason run is realistic, but every game is must-win with the Week 17 clash against the Giants potentially deciding the division.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.desc: Denver has won 17 consecutive one-score games and Bo Nix is playing closer to his 2025 form, though injuries to Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss are concerns. At 7-2 the Broncos are firmly in the AFC playoff picture, with a Week 16 rematch against Buffalo that could decide home-field advantage.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.desc: Detroit has won four straight and improved its defense, allowing 17 or fewer points in three games, with their first game in Germany adding another layer to an already-important week. The Lions sit at 6-2 with a strong two-way profile, though the defense's sustainability against elite postseason competition remains the key question.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.desc: Jordan Love and a dangerous receiver duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden torched New England, and Green Bay's defense has looked stout. At 6-3 the Packers remain in the NFC wild-card mix, but losing NFC North tiebreakers to other conference opponents could become an issue down the stretch.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.desc: Houston has looked dominant at times but remains inconsistent at 3-5, and ESPN says a Week 10 loss to Cleveland would effectively end their season. Writers acknowledge the Texans' potential but are waiting on a string of quality performances before fully believing in them.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.desc: The Colts are in disarray after firing GM Chris Ballard, and Daniel Jones may be on his way out of the starting lineup. At 2-7, Indianapolis belongs near the bottom of every ranking, and writers see little path to relevance before year's end.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.desc: Jacksonville has blown out most opponents under Liam Coen and is pulling away in the AFC South at 6-2, though Bleacher Report notes the Jaguars remain underrated nationally. A Week 14 game against Pittsburgh matters for AFC seeding and could complete a season sweep of the AFC North.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.desc: Kansas City beat the Jets despite a scare for Patrick Mahomes' elbow, and the defense kept them at 6-2 even as the receiving corps remains a weakness. A Week 12 win at Buffalo would put the Chiefs in strong position to chase the AFC's top seed and the AFC West title.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.desc: Los Angeles is winless at 0-8, with offensive struggles under Mike McDaniel and injuries to Ladd McConkey and Justin Herbert piling up. Writers agree the Chargers look like the league's worst team, and their Week 16 game at Miami carries major implications for the No. 1 overall draft pick.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.desc: The Rams are on a three-game win streak with Myles Garrett providing a pass-rush boost, but injuries to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams could force a grinding, low-scoring style. At 5-4 Los Angeles is firmly in the NFC wild-card picture, and a Week 12 game against Green Bay could determine a tiebreaker.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.desc: Kirk Cousins has the Raiders at 4-5 as a bridge quarterback, and writers see the team as still a year away from deep playoff runs. A Week 12 game at Cleveland, before their bye, could determine whether the Raiders stick with Cousins or begin auditions for Fernando Mendoza.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.desc: Miami is 1-7 and writers are pointing toward the future, with Malik Willis looking like a long-term non-answer at quarterback. The Dolphins likely hold a top-three 2027 draft pick, and a Week 16 game against the Chargers could affect their shot at the No. 1 overall selection.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.desc: Minnesota has a championship-caliber defense but inconsistent quarterback play, and Kevin Seifert says every NFC North game is now critical starting with next week's trip to Green Bay. The Vikings sit at 6-2, and writers agree the offense needs trade-deadline help to match the defense's ceiling.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.desc: Drake Maye has been inconsistent and New England's defense struggled in a home loss to Green Bay, but the Patriots are still at 5-4. Writers point to a Week 13 game against Buffalo as a potential AFC East decision point.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.desc: New Orleans has become more aggressive on defense after the bye but has lost three one-score games and needs to close out tight contests. At 3-5 the Saints are still in the NFC South race, with both a Week 17 game at Atlanta and Week 18 at home against Tampa Bay as potential playoff tiebreakers.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.desc: The Giants keep winning despite injuries, sitting at 5-2-1 and leading the NFC East, and writers note John Harbaugh is focused on how the team handles success. A Week 17 game against Dallas could decide the NFC East or playoff seeding.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.desc: New York has lost four straight and writers say a coaching change may be needed to unlock the roster's clear talent. The Jets sit at 2-7, with draft position increasingly the focal point and two top-five picks potentially on the table.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.desc: Philadelphia has lost seven straight, is on its third starting quarterback, and ESPN projects them picking fifth in the 2027 draft. Writers and the team have shifted focus to building toward next season, with head coach Nick Sirianni's future under scrutiny after the bye.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.desc: Pittsburgh has a strong run game, stout defense, and Aaron Rodgers playing well at 6-2, with Bleacher Report noting they need to end a long playoff-win drought. A Week 10 win at Cincinnati would help the Steelers win the AFC North and earn a top-four seed.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.desc: Seattle is efficient on offense but lacks a true punch in the passing game, and the quarterback situation around Drew Lock and an injured Sam Darnold creates uncertainty. The Seahawks sit at 5-4, with ESPN noting a Week 12 loss at San Francisco would hand the 49ers the head-to-head tiebreaker in the NFC West.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.desc: San Francisco dominated the Raiders without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel and sits at 7-1, though writers note those absences will matter more against playoff-caliber competition. A Week 12 home game against Seattle is a chance to effectively claim the NFC West early, given the 49ers' 3-0 division record.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.desc: Tampa Bay has built a strong run-first identity and leads the league in forced turnovers, but Baker Mayfield and the passing offense have been a drag. At 3-6 the Buccaneers face a Week 11 road game at Detroit coming out of the bye, and a 3-7 start would be a very deep hole.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.desc: Tennessee is headed for a fifth consecutive losing season at 1-7, though Cam Ward is showing real development and the offense has quietly improved. A Week 14 win over Indianapolis would complete a sweep, though writers note it could also cost the Titans a top draft position.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.desc: Washington's playoff hopes are fading amid injuries, defensive holes, and poor decision-making, and the Commanders sit at 2-5-1 with Dan Quinn's job under pressure. A Week 10 win at the Giants would provide a tiebreaker, but writers see the team as struggling in the short term.

11.title: Bengals and Rams on the Rise

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.desc: Carson Beck's first start went about as expected against the Rams, with two interceptions and five sacks in a 34-6 loss. Some saw a better game than the box score, and he is now the starter after Gardner Minshew's elbow injury. Arizona heads to Kansas City next.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.desc: Atlanta's 35-13 home loss to Kansas City left writers struck by how little fight the Falcons showed after the trade deadline. Losing Jessie Bates III stung the locker room, and this team swings between beating good teams and getting blown out. The bye arrives with questions about whether Andy Dalton gets a look.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.desc: Baltimore's home loss to the previously winless Chargers was a low point, and Jacoby Brissett's debut did little to move the offense. Derrick Henry managed 10 yards on 10 carries, and Jesse Minter's defense is under scrutiny too. A trip to Carolina is next, with the season on the line.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.desc: Buffalo stays on top after handling the Jets, and the theme is a team that starts slow and still wins easily. Josh Allen's MVP case keeps building, and Greg Rousseau's pass rush gives the defense a real edge. The only quibble is those sluggish starts, with Miami coming to town next.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.desc: Carolina's win over New Orleans was ugly, but it kept the Panthers in the NFC South race, and Chuba Hubbard is the reason. He ran for two scores and caught five passes for 80 yards, and the takeaway is simple: feed him. Baltimore visits next.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.desc: Coming off the bye, Chicago holds steady among the NFC's best, with Luther Burden emerging as a breakout receiver and Jeffery Simmons anchoring the defense. The caution is the division, not the roster, since the NFC North is shaping up as the league's toughest. The Saints visit four days before a showdown with Detroit, and nobody wants a letdown.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.desc: Joe Burrow's 409-yard night in a rout of Pittsburgh has him atop the MVP conversation and Cincinnati atop the AFC North. Boye Mafe's pass rush is quietly backing it up. The open question is whether the offense can evolve when Burrow is not throwing four touchdowns, starting Monday night in Washington.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.desc: Cleveland's win over Houston put the Browns firmly in the AFC playoff picture, and Todd Monken is drawing Coach of the Year talk. Harold Fannin Jr. keeps producing, and Quinshon Judkins scored the winner late. Some rankings still have them in the high teens, but the bye arrives with momentum.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.desc: Dallas scored 40 points and still lost to San Francisco, which says everything about this defense. The pressure on coordinator Christian Parker is intense, and Brian Schottenheimer would not commit to him. George Pickens' three touchdowns were the bright spot, and Tennessee visits next.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.desc: Denver rested on its bye and stays firmly in a loaded AFC race, with rookie Jonah Coleman taking over the backfield. Opinions on the Broncos vary more than on most contenders, with rankings from #2 to #11. Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders come to town before a closing stretch full of big games.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.desc: Detroit routed New England in Munich, but the mood soured with Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL and Jack Campbell also hurt. The offense still looks Super Bowl caliber, while a defense already near the bottom by efficiency is the worry. Tampa Bay visits Sunday, and Kerby Joseph is set to return.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.desc: Green Bay fell hard after Minnesota sacked Jordan Love eight times in a 30-10 loss at home. The read is blunt: the offensive line cannot handle elite fronts, and the run game needs fixing. Christian Watson's career year is the bright spot, and the bye gives them time to regroup.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.desc: Houston's loss to Cleveland may have closed the door on a second-half turnaround. The defense that won games on its own last year is now losing them, and Azeez Al-Shaair went to injured reserve. C.J. Stroud has been sharp, and a Thursday night game with the Colts is next.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.desc: Indianapolis beat Miami, but the win did little to change the mood around a lost season. Daniel Jones takes most of the blame, and some want a look at Anthony Richardson. The Colts visit Houston on Thursday night.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.desc: Jacksonville throttled Tennessee without its two new acquisitions, and the tone is that this is a special season. Parker Washington and Bhayshul Tuten are the breakout stories, and Travis Hunter is making plays everywhere. Some rankings still slot them just behind Buffalo and San Francisco, and a trip to the Giants is next.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.desc: Kansas City is inching back toward the top, and the mood centers on Patrick Mahomes looking like himself again. Rookie Emmett Johnson ran for 101 yards with Kenneth Walker out, and new receiver Josh Downs scored in his debut. Walker's injury is reportedly minor, and Arizona visits next.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.desc: The Chargers finally won, beating Baltimore 23-20 on Monday night behind a revived run game led by Omarion Hampton. Jim Harbaugh's relief was obvious, though questions about Justin Herbert's mood linger. The Jets visit next, a real chance to stack wins.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.desc: The Rams have won four straight by turning into a run-first team, with Blake Corum and Kyren Williams carrying the load. The doubt is how long that holds with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both on injured reserve. A defense led by breakout cornerback Quentin Lake gives them a floor heading into the bye.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.desc: Fernando Mendoza's first start, a 21-13 loss to Seattle, drew a mixed review: poised in the pocket, but limited to short throws for 143 yards. Some questioned the timing of the switch, and Brock Bowers hurt his ankle again. A trip to Denver comes next.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.desc: Miami lost to Indianapolis by two and cut its kicker afterward, sliding to the bottom of the consensus. Kyle McCord showed something in relief of the injured Malik Willis, including a rushing touchdown. A trip to Buffalo is next.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.desc: Kirk Cousins' return ignited Minnesota, and a 30-10 win at Lambeau with eight sacks of Jordan Love has writers talking about a real title shot. The idea is simple: a better offense lets Brian Flores' elite defense play with a lead. A Mexico City date with San Francisco is the first real proof.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.desc: New England took the biggest drop of the week after a 35-10 loss to Detroit, with Drake Maye likely done for the year. A.J. Brown is hurt again, and questions about cohesion and Mike Vrabel's footing are getting louder. The bye arrives with the playoff picture slipping away.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.desc: New Orleans fell 20-17 in Carolina, following a familiar script of sleepwalking through the first half. Tyler Shough has regressed after a strong start, and the Kellen Moore era is under the microscope. Rookie Jordyn Tyson is the bright spot after an 11-catch game, with a trip to Chicago next.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.desc: The Giants lost a close one to Washington on Thursday night, which put a damper on an otherwise positive season. Isaiah Likely has become one of the league's most productive tight ends, and the NFC East is still theirs to control. Jacksonville visits next, after extra days to prepare.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.desc: The Jets dropped a fifth straight game, 31-12 to Buffalo, and Geno Smith left hurt before rookie Cade Klubnik got his first snaps. The frustration is aimed at Aaron Glenn, now seen as the coach most likely to be fired next. Smith is expected to stay the starter for a trip to the Chargers.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.desc: Philadelphia sat on its bye with Joe Milton at quarterback and the season largely gone. Moro Ojomo's growth made the Jordan Davis trade possible, and talk has turned to Nick Sirianni's future. Pittsburgh comes to town next.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.desc: Pittsburgh slid after a 38-18 blowout in Cincinnati, and the critique is that the Steelers cannot win a shootout. Aaron Rodgers' offense works when the defense grinds games down, and that never happened. Jaylen Warren's efficiency is a real asset, and a trip to Philadelphia is a chance to steady things.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.desc: Seattle keeps winning with Drew Lock, who is unbeaten in three starts without an interception, and the defense remains one of the stingiest anywhere. That has started a real debate about whether Sam Darnold should get his job back. The bye comes at a good time, with Seattle still three games behind San Francisco.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.desc: The 49ers hung 46 on Dallas, and writers came away convinced Kyle Shanahan runs the best offense in football, with Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey both dominant. The worry is a defense that gave up 40 to a struggling team. Minnesota's defense in Mexico City is the test that matters next.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.desc: Tampa Bay is 3-6 yet still viewed as the NFC South favorite, thanks to a defense that has led the league in efficiency over the last five weeks. Todd Bowles' unit carries a team whose offense leans on Bucky Irving. Baker Mayfield's foot strain is the worry heading into a trip to Detroit.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.desc: Tennessee lost again, 40-23 to Jacksonville, but Cam Ward's efficient two-touchdown game is giving fans reason for hope in 2027. The Titans are now in line for the first pick after the Chargers won. A trip to Dallas and its struggling defense is next.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.desc: Washington's win over the Giants, sealed by Stefon Diggs' late touchdown, produced the biggest climb of the week. Diggs and Jayden Daniels are clicking, and a weak division keeps an NFC East title in play. Dan Quinn's job is still in question, and Cincinnati visits Monday night.
